**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant**: Sugarcane
- **Affected parts**: Leaves and stem base
- **Key visual features**:
  - Leaves are extensively bleached/straw-colored (cream to pale yellow-white)
  - Clear longitudinal streaks/stripes running parallel to leaf veins along the full leaf length
  - Some leaves retain green coloration at margins/tips while the majority of leaf tissue is bleached
  - Reddish/pink discoloration visible at the stem base
  - Multiple leaves on the plant are severely affected, with a "scalded" appearance

**Reasoning against other classes:**
- **Brown_Spot**: No brown oval/circular lesions visible
- **Grassy_Shoot**: No abnormal proliferation of thin shoots
- **Sett_Rot**: Affects underground sett tissue, not leaf-level symptoms
- **Yellow_Spot**: No distinct yellow blotches/spots
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus**: Mosaic pattern would show irregular yellow-green patches, not longitudinal streaks
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Would show twisted/distorted young leaves
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Primarily causes midrib yellowing, not this extensive streaked bleaching

**Best match — Leaf Scald**: The characteristic white-to-cream pencil-line and broader streaks running longitudinally across the leaves, combined with the extensive straw-colored leaf bleaching (scalding), is the hallmark presentation of *Xanthomonas albilineans* (Leaf Scald). The reddish discoloration at the stalk base is also consistent with the systemic vascular phase of this disease.
